findings.quote: optional Splunk Real User Monitoring ([Splunkbase 5715](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5715)) ... optional Splunk APM Add-on for Splunk Enterprise when Observability traces feed Enterprise indexes.

findings.explanation: The SPL joins on `session_id` across the full 30-day window with no time window, so there is no thirty-minute join; the real attribution risk is session_id mismatch across redirects and the subsearch result limit. Step 2's 'duplicate retries widen totals rather than multiply sessions' also misdescribes `max()` per metric.
findings.quote: Conversion attribution lag: purchases firing beyond conservative thirty-minute joins drop out
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the join as session_id-keyed over 30 days, warn about subsearch row limits for high order volume, and say `max()` keeps the worst value per metric per session so duplicate beacons do not double-count.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `case(lcp_ms<=2500,...,inp_ms<=200,...,1=1,"Poor")` sends sessions where the metric is null to the `1=1` branch, so every session with no LCP beacon, or with no user interaction (web-vitals does not report INP when there is no interaction), is bucketed 'Poor' and `cwv_pass=0`. This inflates the Poor cohort and `revenue_uplift_potential`. Guard with `isnull(x), "No data"` first.

`join type=left session_id [search ... earliest=-30d | stats ... by session_id]` is subject to subsearch result limits (default 50,000 rows); a store with more than 50k ordering sessions in 30 days silently loses purchases, understating conversions. Prefer a single `stats` over both sourcetypes keyed by session_id.
Title says 'Real-Time' but the SPL is a 30-day aggregate and implementation schedules weekly steering extracts; nothing is real-time.

summary: Core Web Vitals thresholds and Apache/NGINX timing facts are accurate and the troubleshooting is rich, but the NGINX add-on is cited with the wrong Splunkbase ID, every exclusion points at an unrelated sibling UC, the SPL buckets sessions with no INP/LCP as 'Poor', and the 'Real-Time' framing contradicts a 30-day weekly report.
